summary: Independent lender evidence materially corroborates the Rincón lithium financing, construction/ramp pathway and critical-mineral supply claim already present in Rio Tinto lineage, without relying on Rio Tinto as the origin.

factors.name: catalystScore
factors.basis: IFC states it supplied a $400m direct loan within a $1.175bn package for the $2.5bn Rincón project; the project targets about 53ktpa battery-grade lithium carbonate over a projected 40-year life, with optimization toward 60ktpa.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: IFC independently describes Rincón as strengthening global critical-mineral supply chains and identifies co-financing from IDB Invest, JBIC and Export Finance Australia.

factors.name: executionEvidence
factors.basis: IFC project disclosure records the project as approved Dec. 4, 2025, signed Mar. 10, 2026 and invested Jun. 1, 2026, providing lender-side execution evidence distinct from issuer announcements.

risks.risk: Rincón remains a greenfield development; financing and lender investment do not prove schedule, full ramp, realized operating economics or commodity-price resilience.
IFC classifies the project Environmental Category A (significant), so environmental/social execution remains material despite financing progress.

unknowns: Full-scale production timing and three-year ramp remain prospective rather than realized.
This evidence does not independently establish current equity valuation or a numeric Earth score.
confidence: high for financing/execution milestones; medium for prospective capacity implications
